title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X → S is a scheme in characteristic p, with relative Frobenius X → X^{(p)}. The margin states two hypotheses: (i) every global relative 1-form is closed, f_*Ω^1_{X/S} = f_*Z^1_{X/S}; (ii) a normalisation, apparently f_*O_{X^{(p)}} ≅ O_S (the margin reading is uncertain). The next page fixes the technical conditions: X → X^{(p)} flat, X → S locally of finite presentation, Ω^1 locally free on geometric fibres.

Construction. Under these conditions the Cartier operator C : Z^1_{X/S} → Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S} is defined. Pushing forward to S gives an O_S-linear map
  ω̲ := f_*Ω^1_{X/S} → f_*Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S}.
Assuming base change, f_*Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S} ≅ (f_*Ω^1_{X/S})^{(p)} = ω̲^{(p)}. This is Grothendieck's 'sous réserve que …'. One obtains a linear map
  C̃ : ω̲ → ω̲^{(p)},
the linearised form of the p^{-1}-linear Cartier–Manin operator on global differentials. Twisting it by powers of Frobenius on S gives C̃^{(p^i)} : ω̲^{(p^i)} → ω̲^{(p^{i+1})}. Composing ν of these gives
  F_*^{(ν)} = C̃^{(p^{ν-1})} ∘ … ∘ C̃^{(p)} ∘ C̃ : ω̲ → ω̲^{(p^ν)}.
If λ ↦ λ^{p^ν} is the identity on O_S (e.g. S = Spec F_{p^ν}), then ω̲^{(p^ν)} = ω̲ and F_*^{(ν)} is an O_S-linear endomorphism of ω̲. This is the usual way of turning the semilinear Cartier–Manin (dual Hasse–Witt) operator over F_q into a linear one by taking its ν-th power.

Logarithmic forms. Let ω be a section with C̃ω = ω^{(p)}, i.e. Cω = ω as forms on X. By Cartier's theorem these are the forms that are locally logarithmic derivatives df/f. Induction gives F^{(ν)}ω = ω^{(p^ν)}, and over F_{p^ν} one gets F_*^{(ν)}ω = ω (boxed): logarithmic global forms are fixed vectors of the linearised iterate.

Marginal NB. f_* could be replaced by R^i f_* (Cartier operator on Hodge cohomology).

Purpose. This prepares the 'second part', following the question on the previous page. That question asks whether a section of an abelian scheme whose reductions at closed points s all come, via Verschiebung, from A_s^{(p)} must have finite order. It is the global-to-local, 'almost all p' setting of the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature philosophy in rank one. The connection d+ω has vanishing p-curvature iff Cω = ω, so the fixed-point condition here is exactly 'p-curvature zero'.
errors: The identification f_*Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S} ≅ (f_*Ω^1_{X/S})^{(p)} needs a base-change hypothesis (e.g. flatness and cohomology commuting with base change). Grothendieck flags this himself ('sous réserve que…'); it is not an error.
The condition is first written as λ ↦ λ^{p^ν} being the identity on O_S^*, later as λ = λ^{p^ν} on O_S. The latter (all of O_S) is what is needed for ω̲^{(p^ν)} = ω̲.
Notation: the composite is called F_*^{(ν)}, although it is built from Cartier operators (the Frobenius-dual direction). This is harmless but potentially confusing.

ideas.what: Linearised Cartier operator on global 1-forms C̃ : f_*Ω^1 → (f_*Ω^1)^{(p)}
ideas.modern_name: Cartier–Manin operator (dual of the Hasse–Witt matrix), relative version
ideas.where_published: Possibly the typescript in this same dossier (Gauss–Manin / Cartier operation)

ideas.what: Iterated composite C̃^{(p^{ν-1})}…C̃ becoming a linear endomorphism over F_{p^ν}
ideas.modern_name: Linearisation of a semilinear operator via its ν-th iterate over F_q

ideas.what: Forms with Cω = ω (locally dlog) are fixed by the iterate F_*^{(ν)}
ideas.modern_name: Logarithmic differentials as fixed points of Cartier; Cartier's theorem; p-curvature of d+ω vanishes iff Cω = ω

ideas.what: Remark that f_* may be replaced by R^i f_*
ideas.modern_name: Cartier operator on Hodge cohomology / higher Hasse–Witt operators

missed.claim: The page sets up linear algebra for a 'second part' that apparently aims at an 'almost all p' algebraicity/torsion statement. This builds on the previous page's question: a section of an abelian scheme whose reduction lies in the image of Verschiebung for all closed points — is it torsion? Here the analogue concerns global 1-forms that are logarithmic mod p. This is the rank-one / commutative-group case of the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture, later treated by Chudnovsky, André and Bost. This page itself contains only routine preparatory computation.
missed.quote: Soit ω une section de ω̲ telle que l'on ait C̃ω = ω^{(p)} … qui est loc. une dérivée logarithmique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's own formulation of the rank-one / abelian-scheme version of the p-curvature philosophy, framed via Verschiebung and the Cartier operator on Hodge cohomology. It is of historical rather than new mathematical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page (linearised iterated Cartier–Manin operator; logarithmic forms as its fixed points) is standard. Its interest lies only in the surrounding programme (the rank-one p-curvature / Verschiebung torsion question), which is known in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'λ ≃ O_{X^{(p)}/S}' is probably a normalisation such as f_*(O_{X^{(p)}}) ≅ O_S (reading uncertain).
Final display: the struck-out symbol before F^{(ν)}ω is a deleted C̃^{(p^ν)}; the corrected formula is F^{(ν)}ω = ω^{(p^ν)}.
Insertion above 'endomorphisme': 'O_S-linéaire, de ω̲'; the underlined phrase is 'un endomorphisme'.
